text:
Adam Fox has 22 points in 18 games, 20 of them assists, and the headlines have caught up. The New York Times ran "If you don’t think Adam Fox is one of the NHL’s best defensemen, you’re not paying attention" this week, and several outlets have him in the Norris race. He won it in 2020-21. After 55 games and 53 points last season, he has played all 18 so far at 22.62 minutes a night.

The best sign is how the ice tilts. Shot attempts are close to even with him on at five-on-five (51%), but the Rangers get 58.68% of the expected goals, the quality of chances. Evolving-Hockey had him ninth among 215 defensemen last season, with the biggest share of his value coming from even-strength defense, and in the 99th percentile for driving play.

If anything, the points undersell him. New York has scored 6.0 fewer goals than its chances deserve with Fox on the ice, which usually swings back. Our range projects 85 points over the full season (71 to 99). He rarely shoots (23 shots so far), so nearly all of it will come as assists.
headline: Adam Fox is back in the Norris conversation
